PASS with caveats. (1) INSTRUMENT IDENTITY (Step 3b). The IRW dictionary Description calls this a 'Body feelings questionnaire FKG', and data/opladen2025_body_checking.py glosses it 'Fragebogen Koerpergefuehl, body feelings questionnaire'. Both are wrong: the 20 items are dysfunctional health- and illness-related beliefs ('Ploetzlich auftretende Gelenkschmerzen koennen eine beginnende Laehmung ankuendigen.', 'Hautroetungen sind ein bedrohliches Zeichen fuer Hautkrebs.'), i.e. the Fragebogen zu Koerper und Gesundheit (FKG; Hiller, Rief, Elefant, Margraf, Kroymann, Leibbrand & Fichter, 1997, Zeitschrift fuer Klinische Psychologie 26(3), 226-234), the standard German measure of catastrophising cognitions about bodily symptoms. There is no instrument called 'Fragebogen Koerpergefuehl'. The dictionary Description should be corrected. This is the same class of error as its sibling opladen2025_wi, whose Description says 'Body image scale WI' for the Whiteley Index (batch_122). (2) THE FKG ATTRIBUTION IS AN INFERENCE, NOT A DEPOSIT STATEMENT. The OSF deposit never expands the abbreviation; it gives column codes FKG_1..FKG_20 with their German wording and value labels and nothing else, and the associated open-access paper (PMC12955302) describes a different, healthy-control sample and does not list these trait questionnaires at all. The attribution rests on four converging facts: the abbreviation, the German language, the item content (health-related catastrophising), the four-point stimmt-voll-und-ganz ladder the FKG uses, and its co-administration with the Whiteley Index -- the Rief/Hiller pairing for hypochondriasis. Note the published FKG has 53 items across five factors, so this is a 20-item SELECTION; the items span several of those factors (e.g. FKG_2 and FKG_17 read as 'Intoleranz koerperlicher Beschwerden', FKG_9 and FKG_16 as 'Koerperliche Schwaeche'/health behaviour), so it is not the 20-item catastrophising factor taken whole, and which selection it is could not be established. No published FKG item list could be located to check the German against; a verbatim-phrase search for FKG_1 returns nothing. item_text is therefore the deposit's own wording, which is what respondents read, rather than a wording checked against the instrument original. (3) item_text_translated carries the deposit's own SHORT English content GLOSS per item ('joint pain as a sign of paralysis'), not a sentence-level translation. The deposit publishes nothing longer in English and no English was generated by IRW. Same shape as opladen2025_wi. option_text_translated, by contrast, IS the deposit's own full English anchor text. (4) instructions and section_prompt are blank because the deposit publishes no FKG instruction text anywhere -- the four OSF files are the raw xlsx, the SPSS/R code PDF, an output PDF and an English audio-material PDF for the experimental task, none of which carry a questionnaire header. Not invented. (5) RIGHTS: no clause reserving a right could be quoted from any rights holder, so this ships under 'silence is permission'. Negative findings, recorded so the next reader does not redo them: the FKG was published as a journal article (Zeitschrift fuer Klinische Psychologie, 1997), not as a fee-licensed test kit; Hogrefe/Testzentrale returns no FKG product (searched 2026-09-20); ZPID's Open Test Archive (testarchiv.eu) returns 404 for it, so it is not deposited there under stated terms; no distribution page for the instrument could be found at all, let alone one carrying a fee, a non-commercial term, a permission-required term or a no-redistribution bar. No register row was written: SKILL.md forbids a round writing a 'ship' verdict into instrument_rights_register.csv, and there is no block to record. Worth flagging to the orchestrator that this is silence rather than a positive grant, and that the same open question was left standing over its sibling opladen2025_wi (the GESIS ZIS lead, still unresolved) -- the FKG has no equivalent lead, because no archive entry for it exists. (6) A coverage gap that is a property of the data, not of this extraction: FKG_16 has no resp=1 observation (0/19/69/122 over levels 1-4). The option row for resp=1 is shipped anyway, because the instrument offered the anchor; audit_batch.R may report the gap. (7) VERIFICATION: mapping_basis is data_labels and the item code IS the source column name, so Step 5b exempts this table -- but a decisive check was cheap and was run anyway, and verify_opladen2025_fkg.R re-runs it. All 80 item x response-level counts computed from the deposit's own spreadsheet reproduce the live IRW table exactly (0 mismatching cells), and the 20 count vectors are mutually distinct, so the check separates every item from every other. Evidence: the deposit's own SPSS syntax (Data - Codes.pdf, osf.io/58xb9) heads the FKS block '*recoding Questionnaire of bodydysmorphic symptoms (FKS)*' and computes mean_specific_BDD from reFKS_1,4-15 and mean_assoc_BDD from reFKS_16,17,18; the item content is appearance preoccupation, mirror checking, appearance comparison, reassurance seeking, cosmetic surgery and appearance-related suicidality. The Description should be corrected to name the FKS as a body dysmorphic symptom screener. NOTE this is the sibling table to opladen2025_fkg in the same batch and the same source file; FKS and FKG are DIFFERENT instruments and were checked against each other -- FKG_1..FKG_20 in the same Readme are dysfunctional illness/health cognitions ('Ploetzlich auftretende Gelenkschmerzen koennen eine beginnende Laehmung ankuendigen'), on a 1-4 stimmt-voll-und-ganz..stimmt-nicht scale, while FKS is appearance concern on a 1-5 ueberhaupt-nicht..sehr-stark scale.
